about: How the interviewers' voices say words they get wrong (EC-11.11). An entry is here only because the voice said the term and Whisper did not hear it back, and its respelling WAS heard back (research/lexicon/probe.py). `exact`: only that casing (an acronym). Names (2026-10-11): an Indian name read with English letter rules comes back right from Whisper and still sounds foreign, so the read-back test cannot judge them; they are respelled by ear.

entries.why: In 'Doctor Raghavan, over to you.' this voice was heard as 'Aghwawan'; 'Raghaavan' came back right. The other six voices say 'Raghavan' as written and each respelling made some of them worse, so this one is for this voice only (research/lexicon/handover.json).
